newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power mostly higher on chill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power mostly higher on chill.

text.p: Day-ahead wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast were higher Wednesday, extending Tuesday's gain on a blistering chill that has blanketed the region since Monday.
Thursday's temperatures were predicted to peak at 20-30 degrees Fahrenheit and bottom in the single digits with increasing winds and possibility of snow as the week progresses.
Although price assessments rose from Tuesday's levels, volume of transactions was modest, market sources said.
"The offers are coming up. The bids are staying where they are," said a Houston power marketer.
There was still ample nuclear and coal generation in the region to meet the pickup in weather-related load, traders and marketers said.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Thursday delivery in the eastern part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) climbed to $29.00-$31.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Tuesday's $27.50-$31.00.
Quote for off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in eastern NYPP narrowed to $21.00-$22.00 from $19.50-$22.50 Tuesday.

In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Thursday slipped to $24.00-$25.00 from Tuesday's $25.50-$27.00, reflecting weaker import demand from the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect region.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Thursday was valued at $15.00-$16.00, lower than Tuesday's range of $16.00-$16.50.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for day-ahead delivery at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border firmed to $34.00-$35.00/MWh from $31.00-$34.00 Tuesday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was valued at $21.50-$23.00, a slightly tighter range than Tuesday's $21.00-$23.00.
